verses.author: model_A
verses.text: A boat leaves the harbor before anyone is awake to see it go.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
wake still ripples
long after the water
forgets the shape of the hull

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
gulls circle the empty pier
tracing a shape
no one taught them to remember

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
morning fog swallows
the shoreline whole—
even forgetting needs a shape

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
a hand reaches into fog
finds nothing
and calls that touching too

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the empty hand
still knows the shape of holding—
a bowl waiting for rain

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
rain fills the bowl
that never asked for water—
this is what enough looks like

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
overflow finds the crack
already in the clay—
enough was never the point

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the crack widens into a mouth
and the bowl learns to say
what water taught it

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
morning finds the mouth still open
saying nothing—
this too is a kind of speech

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
silence pools where words would sit
the bowl keeps its counsel now
and the light says nothing back

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
a bird lands on the rim
tests the quiet with one note
then leaves it unbroken

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the note hangs where the bird was
smaller than silence
just enough to remember by

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the kettle takes up that same pitch
boiling over into steam
before it can be kept

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
steam blurs the window's edge
what was clear
learns to hold nothing steady

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
i wipe a circle in the fog
just enough to see
that the yard forgot me too
